title: Egg, whole, fried with cooking spray

content.title: About
content.content: Eggs are a nutrient‑dense food produced by chickens. When fried with cooking spray, most vitamins and minerals are retained while added fat is kept to a minimum.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: An egg contains all essential amino acids, making it a complete protein source.
The yolk is rich in vitamin D, which is hard to obtain from many other foods.
Cooking spray is usually based on plant oils and allows precise control of fat amount.
A typical large chicken egg weighs about 50 g.
Eggs can be stored in the refrigerator for 4–5 weeks.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: One large egg provides roughly 6 g of protein, essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs supply vitamin B12, riboflavin (B2) and biotin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Choline
items.content: Choline in the yolk is important for liver function and brain health.

items.title: Lutein and zeaxanthin
items.content: These carotenoids promote eye health and may reduce the risk of age‑related macular degeneration.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Eggs contain virtually no carbs, making them suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: The yolk contains cholesterol; people with high cholesterol levels should monitor yolk intake.

items.title: Risk of salmonella
items.content: Undercooked eggs can harbor Salmonella bacteria. Cooking until fully set greatly reduces this risk.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fry the egg over medium heat using cooking spray until desired doneness—sunny side up, over easy, or fully set. Serve with whole‑grain toast, vegetables, or add to salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep eggs in their original carton in the refrigerator at 1–4 °C. Do not wash them before storage to preserve the natural protective coating. Use within 3–4 weeks.
